title: Hold a liquor licence to sell alcohol
what: Hold a liquor licence (or permit) of the right type before selling or supplying alcohol; cafes and restaurants usually need an on-premises or restaurant licence.

sources.title: Liquor Licensing Act 1997 (SA)
sources.publisher: Official register text via the Open Australian Legal Corpus
sources.quote: A person who sells liquor without being licensed under this Act to do so (or who sells liquor under a licence that is suspended) is guilty of an offence.

assessment.summary: Selling alcohol needs a liquor licence, with approvals, fees and conditions on how and when the venue trades.

marks.reason: A licence, approvals and fees are needed before selling alcohol.
Trading hours and licence conditions limit how licensed venues compete.
